purpose.p: How to run Kajenn Press with Docker: on a workstation with local S3 storage, on a server behind nginx with external buckets, with Help me, and how to run its tests. The step-by-step installation of the Hetzner host is deploy/docker/HETZNER.md.

list.item: Docker with Compose, and this repository checked out.
On a server: an S3-compatible service with two buckets with versioning, a reverse proxy with TLS, DNS for the administration's name.

step.title: Run it on a workstation
step.code: cp deploy/docker/.env.example deploy/docker/.env docker compose -f deploy/docker/compose.yaml --profile demo up -d --build docker compose -f deploy/docker/compose.yaml exec websites cat /secrets/operator_password

row.cell: Generates the local credentials once: storage users, operator password, MCP token, and one private-link secret written to both the websites and the site-server volumes.
Local S3 storage; creates the buckets sources and releases with versioning, a read-write user for websites and a user for the site server that reads only releases.
Administration, REST and MCP, render worker, on port 8875: http://kpress.localhost:8875/admin/, user operator.
Publishes the example site through MCP.
Serves the published sites on port 8877: http://press.localhost:8877/.

step.p: down keeps volumes; down -v deletes working copies, buckets and credentials.

step.title: Run it on a server
step.p: Set KPRESS_SCHEME=https, the administration's name in KPRESS_MANAGEMENT_HOST, and in KPRESS_TRUSTED_PROXIES the address the proxy connects from: websites answers only requests whose scheme and host match the administration's origin, and reads the scheme from X-Forwarded-Proto only from a trusted address. deploy/docker/nginx-kpress.conf is the nginx configuration of the Hetzner host.
With external buckets, add compose.external-s3.yaml; it does not start RustFS nor the demo services and reads:

row.cell: The source bucket; empty turns the site operations off.
Host directory with the files access and secret, mounted read-only.

step.p: websites refuses to start with a bucket whose versioning is not enabled.

step.title: Prepare a server for published sites
step.p: A server that serves published sites runs the site server (the kajenn-child image) on 127.0.0.1:8877 and the server agent, behind nginx, Caddy or Traefik already installed. On a Debian or Ubuntu host with Docker, as root:

The script creates the user kpress-agent, installs the agent in /opt/kpress-agent with its systemd unit, the sudoers lines of the chosen proxy only, a new token in /etc/kpress-agent/token, and the site server unit with its environment in /etc/kpress-site. It starts nothing and prints what is left:

list.item: in agent.env, the manager's address (AGENT_ALLOWED) and the agent's certificate and key; for nginx, the ACME e-mail;
in site.env, the server's name as registered and the release bucket; in secrets, its read-only keys and the private-link secret;
the token copied to the manager as <agent_tokens>/<server>.token;
the proxy: nginx includes /etc/nginx/kpress.d/*.conf; Caddy uses deploy/agent/Caddyfile; Traefik watches /etc/traefik/kpress;
the firewall: 80 and 443 open, the agent's port 8890 only from the manager.

step.p: Then register the server on the manager with server_add (name, addresses, agent URL) and start both units.

step.title: Enable Help me
step.p: Put the installation's Claude API key in a private file readable by websites, name it in KPRESS_HELP_KEY_FILE, and add compose.help.yaml to every Compose command. The key is never generated and never enters a volume. Without it, the Help me pane says Help me is not configured.

step.title: Run the tests
step.p: The full suite needs a render interpreter and a disposable S3 endpoint; the administration tests an interpreter with the admin extra; the Docker tests drive the composition and delete its volumes.
step.code: KAJENN_RENDER_PYTHON=/path/to/render/python KAJENN_RELEASE_S3=/path/to/s3.json .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests KAJENN_DOCKER=1 PYTHONPATH=src .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --import-mode=importlib tests/docker
step.p: KAJENN_RELEASE_S3 is a private JSON file with endpoint_url, access_key and secret_key. The live Help me tests run only with KAJENN_HELP_LIVE=1 and cost tokens.

rules.rule: Run tests/docker on a server with a real installation.

rule.why: Pages and sources are read and restored by version.

rules.rule: Enable versioning on both buckets before the first start.

rule.why: Project-wide keys would let a site server read the sources.

rules.rule: Give site servers keys that read the source bucket.

rule.why: The agent changes the proxy's configuration.

rules.rule: Expose the agent's port to any address but the manager's.

limits.limit: The hashed dependency locks target aarch64 Linux.
Kajenn has no ACME client: TLS comes from the reverse proxy.

facts.fact: The composition starts websites on 8875 and, with the demo profile, the site publisher and the site server on 8877.
One private-link secret is written to both the websites and the site-server volumes.
websites refuses a source or release bucket whose versioning is not enabled.
Help me is configured only when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_FILE names a file.
In a Debian container, the script installed the agent for nginx and for Caddy with the proxy's sudoers lines only; the installed agent answered 200 with its token and 401 with another.
The external-bucket composition writes sources and releases to the given buckets.
